clue.text: It may mean junk ends up as junk!

definitions.text: It may mean junk ends up as junk!

parts.words: It may mean junk ends up as junk!
parts.note: a junk is a Chinese sailing boat; when such a vessel is lost at sea, it ends up as worthless junk

explanation.surface: A wry remark about clutter that is fit only for the scrap heap.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'junk' is the Chinese sailing boat, the second is rubbish: a boat that comes to grief becomes wreckage.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruined vessel becomes debris, so the whole clue describes the loss of a boat at sea.

clue.text: Blissful place in the avenue

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the run of words the avenue

explanation.surface: A street described as paradise, perhaps by an estate agent.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise, the abode of the blessed, is the archetypal place of bliss.

clue.text: Quiet editor, worker who pays attention to good grammar?

definitions.text: who pays attention to good grammar?
definitions.note: a noun phrase in sense: one who fusses over grammatical correctness

parts.note: P is piano, the musical marking for quiet
an ant is the crossword's stock worker insect

explanation.surface: A quiet editor described as a stickler for correct usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stickler for rules and small details, such as correct grammar, is the classic nitpicker.

clue.text: Declaim as English Conservative joining in ceremony

indicators.note: joining in says the English and Conservative letters enter the word for ceremony

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: An English Tory delivering a speech at some formal occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: To declaim is to speak aloud in a rhetorical way, as one does when delivering a poem from memory.

clue.text: Bill coming up — what is charged is something fanciful

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the bill's letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
the price is what a seller charges

explanation.surface: A bill arrives showing a fanciful charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' tempts as a man's name or a beak; here it is an account, and 'coming up' suits a down light read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A whim or sudden fancy is something fanciful, a notion with no solid reason behind it.

clue.text: Is husband getting on held in serious ignominy?

indicators.note: held in says the run of short pieces is enclosed by the word for serious

parts.note: dour means stern and serious
taken as written
on, as in getting on a bus, means aboard

explanation.surface: A question whether a husband's progress is held in grave disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean public shame and loss of reputation; they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Leader of society wants fairness organised without any frills

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of society
organised says the letters of fairness are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A society leader calls for fairness to be organised.
explanation.walkthrough: S from 'Leader of society', then 'organised' rearranges FAIRNESS into ANSSERIF.
explanation.definitionFit: A typeface of this kind lacks the small finishing strokes on letters, so it is literally without frills.

clue.text: Rob and Pete dread being made to look silly

indicators.note: being made to look silly says the letters of Pete dread are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Rob and Pete are worried about being made fools of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rob' looks like a man's name beside Pete; it is the verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To plunder or lay waste is to rob, a formal synonym for stealing by force.

clue.text: Something not what it seems? This person's about to get very cross

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the contraction is read backwards

parts.note: the setter refers to themself; this person is = I'M
to rage is to get very angry

explanation.surface: Someone warns that they are about to become furious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'on the point of', but it is the turnaround signal; 'This person' is the setter speaking of themself.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion, like water seen in a desert, is something that is not what it appears to be.

clue.text: Lights by promontory shown in picture

parts.note: to light on something is to alight, i.e. land
a cape is a headland or promontory

explanation.surface: Lamps beside a headland shown in a painting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lights' is a verb (alights, comes to rest), not lamps.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting of rural scenery is a common kind of picture, a genre of art.

clue.text: Hunter's drink — not the first

definitions.meaning: one who pursues, like a hunter
a drink taken straight after another, so never the first one

explanation.surface: A huntsman's tipple, consumed after something else.
explanation.definitionFit: One who pursues is a hunter; and a follow-up drink, such as beer after whisky, has the same name.

clue.text: Composer in Swiss city with beer mug

parts.note: Bern is the Swiss capital
a stein is a large earthenware beer mug

explanation.surface: A composer drinking from a tankard in Switzerland.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonard Bernstein was an American composer and conductor, known for West Side Story.

clue.text: Article penned by a foreign Socialist is not perused

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: penned by says the article is enclosed by the word for a socialist

parts.note: a red is a socialist or communist
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A piece written by a foreign left-winger goes unread.
explanation.definitionFit: A text that has not been perused has simply never been looked through by anyone.

clue.text: Someone having agents to sort out party mess

indicators.note: sort out says the letters of party mess are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone with staff to clear up after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agents' suggests helpers or cleaners; here they are spies.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of an espionage network runs a team of secret agents.

clue.text: English partygoers? They get into the groove

parts.note: ravers are people who go to wild parties

explanation.surface: English party animals getting into the rhythm of the music.
explanation.definitionFit: Craftsmen who incise designs into metal or wood literally cut grooves, so they get into the groove.

clue.text: With stress beginning to spread around, I had bad things happening

indicators.note: around says the word for stress goes round the contraction of I had

parts.note: accent is stress on a syllable
ID is the contraction I'd

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of spread

explanation.surface: As tension spreads, someone reports a run of misfortunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' belongs to the container, not to 'spread': the stress word goes round the contraction for 'I had'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mishaps and unfortunate events are unplanned harmful occurrences, i.e. bad things happening.

clue.text: Edmund falling over in pit

indicators.note: falling over says the name is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: Ned is a short form of Edmund

explanation.surface: A man named Edmund tumbles into a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair or hollow where an animal lives is a pit or hole, as in a lions' lair.

clue.text: One day rising to find dampness

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Wed is short for Wednesday, one day of the week

explanation.surface: Getting up one morning to find everything damp.
explanation.definitionFit: Morning moisture condensed on grass is a light dampness.

clue.text: Sign of approval in words regularly trotted out

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of in words is taken

explanation.surface: Approval given in phrases repeated by rote.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the second, fourth and sixth letters of 'in words' gives N, O, D.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip of the head is a common gesture showing agreement or approval.

clue.text: Criticise a revolutionary for grand manner

parts.note: to pan is to criticise harshly
Che Guevara is the stock revolutionary

explanation.surface: Faulting a rebel for putting on airs.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamboyant style and confident flair amount to a grand manner.

clue.text: Someone who sees what you can see

definitions.text: Someone who sees what you can see

parts.words: Someone who sees what you can see
parts.note: the eyes are what you see with; a specialist who examines eyes sees them

explanation.definitionFit: An eye doctor examines patients' eyes, the very organs by which they see.

clue.text: Black bird rolls over in this bundle

indicators.note: rolls over says the bird's name is turned round, read backwards

parts.note: a daw, or jackdaw, is a black bird of the crow family

explanation.surface: A black bird rolling around in a heap of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A compact roll of banknotes or a pad of material is a bundle.

clue.text: Irritability in an east Texas city

indicators.note: in says the word for irritability sits inside an

parts.note: bile means bad temper or irritability
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Bad temper found in an eastern part of Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'east Texas' tempts as one region, but 'east' gives the final E.
explanation.definitionFit: Abilene is a city in west-central Texas, famous in cattle-drive history.

clue.text: Saint in ruin needing money

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A holy figure fallen into poverty and in need of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: St Martin of Tours is a well-known saint, patron of soldiers.

clue.text: Author with obstacle, not finishing

indicators.note: not finishing says the last letter of the word for obstacle is dropped

parts.note: a barrier is an obstacle

explanation.surface: A writer faces a hurdle and fails to complete the work.
explanation.definitionFit: J. M. Barrie was the Scottish author who wrote Peter Pan.

clue.text: Drink repeatedly being knocked over leads to grumble

indicators.note: knocked over in a down entry turns the letters upside down, reading backwards
repeatedly says the drink appears twice in succession

parts.note: rum is a drink

explanation.surface: Drinks keep being spilt, which makes someone complain.
explanation.definitionFit: A low muttered complaint is a grumble, as in a murmur of discontent.

clue.text: Note put up: 'We need this for cheese-making'

indicators.note: put up in a down entry means the letters go upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote

explanation.surface: A notice pinned up by cheesemakers listing what they need.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' looks like a written message; it is a banknote.
explanation.definitionFit: This curdling agent, from calves' stomachs, is what makes milk set for cheese.

clue.text: Terrible US baddies must be set free from wrong ideas

indicators.note: terrible says the letters of US baddies are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: American villains need to be corrected about their mistaken beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cured of a false belief is to be set free from mistaken notions.

clue.text: Veto is exercised in council

indicators.note: exercised says the letters of veto is are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: A veto used during a meeting of a governing body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exercised' seems to mean used, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: In Russian the word means council; elected councils governed the old USSR.

clue.text: Carpet material by edge and at the back

indicators.note: at the back says and comes after the other pieces

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A rug's fabric described by its border and back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' is the verb: to carpet someone is British slang for scolding them.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is to haul them up for a dressing-down, i.e. to scold.

clue.text: Blunders made by English bishop at back of basilica

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

indicators.note: the back of a word is its last letter, here of basilica

explanation.surface: Mistakes made by an English bishop in a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of printing mistakes in a book is a list of blunders, Latin for errors.

clue.text: See red and act violently, bringing 6

definitions.note: 6-down read as a verb: to treat with disgrace

indicators.note: violently says the letters of see red and act are flung into a new order

explanation.surface: Losing one's temper and lashing out, bringing disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 6-down used as a verb, to violate something sacred.
explanation.definitionFit: To profane a sacred place is to bring shame upon it, a verb synonym.
